title: Information Retrieval
topics: Nature and scope of retrieval systems

items.q: Tokenisation may be defined as
o: the breaking of running text into separate words before they are stored
a stored query that can be run again later without being retyped
the drawing of index entries directly out of the words of the title or text
the combining of search terms with AND, OR and NOT to include or exclude records
items.s: Tokenisation: the breaking of running text into separate words before they are stored. The other options describe Derived indexing, Saved search, Boolean logic.

items.q: Which term is described by “the use of brackets to settle which parts of a compound query are handled first”?
o: Boolean OR
Boolean logic
Truncation
Nesting
items.s: Nesting is the use of brackets to settle which parts of a compound query are handled first.

items.q: Truncation may be defined as
o: the agreement of different indexers, or of one indexer at different times, on the terms chosen
an approach that estimates the chance that a document is wanted from the terms it shares with the query
the cutting of a word to its stem, with a symbol, so that every ending is matched
the measured extent to which two people assign the same terms to the same item
items.s: Truncation: the cutting of a word to its stem, with a symbol, so that every ending is matched. The other options describe Consistency, Inter-indexer agreement, Probabilistic model.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Crawler.
o: the tendency for a search that finds more of the relevant material to return more unwanted material as well
a class of more limited meaning that falls inside a wider class
a program that follows links across the web and copies pages back for indexing
the agreement of different indexers, or of one indexer at different times, on the terms chosen
items.s: Crawler: a program that follows links across the web and copies pages back for indexing. The other options describe Recall-precision trade-off, Consistency, Narrower heading.

items.q: All of the following belong to Web search and discovery tools EXCEPT
o: Factual databank
Crawler
Search engine
Inverted file
items.s: Every other option belongs to Web search and discovery tools. “Factual databank” belongs to Nature and scope of retrieval systems, not Web search and discovery tools.

items.q: The statement “the drawing of index entries directly out of the words of the title or text” describes which of the following?
o: Assignment indexing
Consistency
Derived indexing
Depth of indexing
items.s: Derived indexing is the drawing of index entries directly out of the words of the title or text.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Repository.
o: the operator that keeps only records in which every joined term is present
the choosing of terms from a ready list to stand for the content of an item
an online store of an institution's own output, made openly searchable
the adjustment of a query after the enquirer marks some early results as useful
items.s: Repository: an online store of an institution's own output, made openly searchable. The other options describe Assignment indexing, Boolean AND, Relevance feedback.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Nesting.
o: all the records a given search returned
the use of brackets to settle which parts of a compound query are handled first
an approach that estimates the chance that a document is wanted from the terms it shares with the query
one complete entry in a file, made up of several separate fields
items.s: Nesting: the use of brackets to settle which parts of a compound query are handled first. The other options describe Probabilistic model, Record, Retrieved set.

items.q: The statement “a way of scoring closeness by treating each document and the request as arrows in a shared field of index words” describes which of the following?
o: Geometric similarity
Relevance feedback
Probabilistic model
Clustering
items.s: Geometric similarity is a way of scoring closeness by treating each document and the request as arrows in a shared field of index words.

items.q: Search engine may be defined as
o: the share of the items brought back that were in fact relevant
the operator that keeps records in which any one of the joined terms appears
the use of brackets to settle which parts of a compound query are handled first
a service that crawls pages, stores an index of them and answers queries from that index
items.s: Search engine: a service that crawls pages, stores an index of them and answers queries from that index. The other options describe Boolean OR, Nesting, Precision.

items.q: The statement “a heading that is neither wider nor narrower but is close enough to be worth linking” describes which of the following?
o: Related term
Broader heading
Entry term
Natural language
items.s: Related term is a heading that is neither wider nor narrower but is close enough to be worth linking.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Saved search?
o: the breaking of running text into separate words before they are stored
a store of descriptions of writings rather than of the writings themselves
the measured extent to which two people assign the same terms to the same item
a stored query that can be run again later without being retyped
items.s: Saved search: a stored query that can be run again later without being retyped. The other options describe Inter-indexer agreement, Tokenisation, Bibliographic file.

items.q: Which term is described by “the network of links among terms that shows how each is connected to the others”?
o: Scope note
Controlled vocabulary
Syndetic structure
Preferred term
items.s: Syndetic structure is the network of links among terms that shows how each is connected to the others.

items.q: The statement “the placing of results in an order that reflects their estimated usefulness to the enquirer” describes which of the following?
o: Geometric similarity
Relevance feedback
Relevance ranking
Best match
items.s: Relevance ranking is the placing of results in an order that reflects their estimated usefulness to the enquirer.

items.q: The statement “the searching of many separate collections at once through a single interface” describes which of the following?
o: Inverted file
Discovery layer
Crawler
Federated search
items.s: Federated search is the searching of many separate collections at once through a single interface.

items.q: Which term is described by “a method that begins with one good record and uses its terms or references to find more”?
o: Field searching
Alert
Saved search
Citation pearl growing
items.s: Citation pearl growing is a method that begins with one good record and uses its terms or references to find more.

items.q: Which term is described by “a record that genuinely answers the need, as judged by an assessor”?
o: Relevant item
Recall-precision trade-off
Relevance judgement
Noise
items.s: Relevant item is a record that genuinely answers the need, as judged by an assessor.

items.q: Limiter may be defined as
o: a setting that restricts results by language, date, format or availability
one complete entry in a file, made up of several separate fields
the grouping of similar records together so that a large result set becomes easier to scan
an online store of an institution's own output, made openly searchable
items.s: Limiter: a setting that restricts results by language, date, format or availability. The other options describe Clustering, Record, Repository.

items.q: Miss may be defined as
o: the one form chosen from a group of synonyms to stand for the idea in a file
a relevant item that the search failed to bring back
one complete entry in a file, made up of several separate fields
the unwanted material that appears among the results of a search
items.s: Miss: a relevant item that the search failed to bring back. The other options describe Preferred term, Record, Noise.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Index term?
o: a word or phrase chosen from a document to represent its content in the file
a measure that gives less weight to a word appearing in very many documents
the operator that removes from the result every record containing the excluded term
a single front end that searches the catalogue, the repositories and the subscribed databases together
items.s: Index term: a word or phrase chosen from a document to represent its content in the file. The other options describe Inverse document frequency, Discovery layer, Boolean NOT.

items.q: The statement “searching that works from the meaning of a request rather than from the exact words typed” describes which of the following?
o: Natural language query
Open access
Semantic search
Linked data
items.s: Semantic search is searching that works from the meaning of a request rather than from the exact words typed.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Retrieved set?
o: the person who writes the summary that accompanies a record in a file
a structured file of records that can be searched and updated independently of the programs using it
all the records a given search returned
the cutting of a word to its stem, with a symbol, so that every ending is matched
items.s: Retrieved set: all the records a given search returned. The other options describe Truncation, Database, Abstractor.

items.q: The statement “the one form chosen from a group of synonyms to stand for the idea in a file” describes which of the following?
o: Syndetic structure
Scope note
Preferred term
Narrower heading
items.s: Preferred term is the one form chosen from a group of synonyms to stand for the idea in a file.

items.q: The statement “a store that keeps the whole of each document and searches inside it” describes which of the following?
o: Record
Factual databank
Full text file
Retrieval system
items.s: Full text file is a store that keeps the whole of each document and searches inside it.
items.t: Nature and scope of retrieval systems

items.q: Recommender system may be defined as
o: a store of descriptions of writings rather than of the writings themselves
the number of times a given word occurs inside one document
a method that starts with a large set and narrows it step by step
a service that suggests items from what a person has used before or what similar people used
items.s: Recommender system: a service that suggests items from what a person has used before or what similar people used. The other options describe Term frequency, Bibliographic file, Successive fractions.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Citation pearl growing?
o: the planned sequence of steps by which a topic is searched in a database
the assignment of terms to items by a program rather than by a person
a method that begins with one good record and uses its terms or references to find more
the choosing of terms from a ready list to stand for the content of an item
items.s: Citation pearl growing: a method that begins with one good record and uses its terms or references to find more. The other options describe Search strategy, Machine indexing, Assignment indexing.

items.q: Which term is described by “a method that starts with a large set and narrows it step by step”?
o: Concept block
Successive fractions
Most specific first
Search strategy
items.s: Successive fractions is a method that starts with a large set and narrows it step by step.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Indexing?
o: the intellectual work of deciding what an item is about and expressing that in the language of the system
a record that genuinely answers the need, as judged by an assessor
a symbol standing in for one or more unknown letters inside a search word
the adjustment of a query after the enquirer marks some early results as useful
items.s: Indexing: the intellectual work of deciding what an item is about and expressing that in the language of the system. The other options describe Wildcard, Relevance feedback, Relevant item.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Entry term.
o: a synonym or variant recorded in a list only to send the searcher to the chosen form
a structured file of records that can be searched and updated independently of the programs using it
all the records a given search returned
the share of all the relevant items in a file that the search actually brought back
items.s: Entry term: a synonym or variant recorded in a list only to send the searcher to the chosen form. The other options describe Database, Recall, Retrieved set.

items.q: Which term is described by “the one form chosen from a group of synonyms to stand for the idea in a file”?
o: Preferred term
Scope note
Controlled vocabulary
Related term
items.s: Preferred term is the one form chosen from a group of synonyms to stand for the idea in a file.

items.q: The statement “the measured extent to which two people assign the same terms to the same item” describes which of the following?
o: Inter-indexer agreement
Consistency
Abstractor
Indexing
items.s: Inter-indexer agreement is the measured extent to which two people assign the same terms to the same item.

items.q: Which term is described by “the measured extent to which two people assign the same terms to the same item”?
o: Consistency
Inter-indexer agreement
Derived indexing
Precision of indexing
items.s: Inter-indexer agreement is the measured extent to which two people assign the same terms to the same item.

items.q: The statement “a class of wider meaning to which a narrower class belongs” describes which of the following?
o: Broader heading
Preferred term
Natural language
Scope note
items.s: Broader heading is a class of wider meaning to which a narrower class belongs.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Discovery layer?
o: a single front end that searches the catalogue, the repositories and the subscribed databases together
a store of discrete values such as prices or properties, searched for the values themselves
an approach that estimates the chance that a document is wanted from the terms it shares with the query
the one form chosen from a group of synonyms to stand for the idea in a file
items.s: Discovery layer: a single front end that searches the catalogue, the repositories and the subscribed databases together. The other options describe Factual databank, Preferred term, Probabilistic model.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Alert?
o: the publishing of descriptions as web identifiers that other systems can follow
a service that runs a stored query at intervals and reports anything newly added
a word or phrase chosen from a document to represent its content in the file
a store that keeps the whole of each document and searches inside it
items.s: Alert: a service that runs a stored query at intervals and reports anything newly added. The other options describe Index term, Linked data, Full text file.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Discovery layer?
o: a fixed set of documents, queries and agreed judgements used to compare systems
the extent to which every topic touched on in an item is given a term
the operator that keeps records in which any one of the joined terms appears
a single front end that searches the catalogue, the repositories and the subscribed databases together
items.s: Discovery layer: a single front end that searches the catalogue, the repositories and the subscribed databases together. The other options describe Boolean OR, Exhaustivity, Test collection.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Precision?
o: one element of a topic, around which synonyms are gathered before they are joined
the decision of an assessor that a particular record does or does not answer a query
the planned sequence of steps by which a topic is searched in a database
the share of the items brought back that were in fact relevant
items.s: Precision: the share of the items brought back that were in fact relevant. The other options describe Concept block, Search strategy, Relevance judgement.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Depth of indexing.
o: all the records a given search returned
the average number of terms given to each item in a file
the limiting of a search to one part of the record, such as the title or the year
the ordinary words of a subject as writers use them, without any approved list
items.s: Depth of indexing: the average number of terms given to each item in a file. The other options describe Retrieved set, Field searching, Natural language.

items.q: The statement “a class of more limited meaning that falls inside a wider class” describes which of the following?
o: Narrower heading
Syndetic structure
Natural language
Entry term
items.s: Narrower heading is a class of more limited meaning that falls inside a wider class.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Boolean logic?
o: a system rule that records are returned in order of how well each resembles the query
the combining of search terms with AND, OR and NOT to include or exclude records
a heading that is neither wider nor narrower but is close enough to be worth linking
the person who writes the summary that accompanies a record in a file
items.s: Boolean logic: the combining of search terms with AND, OR and NOT to include or exclude records. The other options describe Abstractor, Best match, Related term.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Relevance feedback?
o: the adjustment of a query after the enquirer marks some early results as useful
the set of very common function words that a system ignores when it builds an index
the process of finding, within a store of recorded material, the items that answer a stated need
the drawing of index entries directly out of the words of the title or text
items.s: Relevance feedback: the adjustment of a query after the enquirer marks some early results as useful. The other options describe Information retrieval, Stop list, Derived indexing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Geometric similarity.
o: the extent to which every topic touched on in an item is given a term
the reduction of a word to its base form so that its variants are treated as one
a way of scoring closeness by treating each document and the request as arrows in a shared field of index words
the one form chosen from a group of synonyms to stand for the idea in a file
items.s: Geometric similarity: a way of scoring closeness by treating each document and the request as arrows in a shared field of index words. The other options describe Stemming, Exhaustivity, Preferred term.

items.q: Which term is described by “the agreement of different indexers, or of one indexer at different times, on the terms chosen”?
o: Inter-indexer agreement
Consistency
Abstractor
Derived indexing
items.s: Consistency is the agreement of different indexers, or of one indexer at different times, on the terms chosen.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Stop list?
o: the process of finding, within a store of recorded material, the items that answer a stated need
the set of very common function words that a system ignores when it builds an index
the adjustment of a query after the enquirer marks some early results as useful
a store of discrete values such as prices or properties, searched for the values themselves
items.s: Stop list: the set of very common function words that a system ignores when it builds an index. The other options describe Relevance feedback, Factual databank, Information retrieval.

items.q: All of the following belong to Nature and scope of retrieval systems EXCEPT
o: Indexing
Information retrieval
Retrieval system
Database
items.s: Every other option belongs to Nature and scope of retrieval systems. “Indexing” belongs to Indexing practice, not Nature and scope of retrieval systems.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Truncation.
o: the reduction of a word to its base form so that its variants are treated as one
a service that crawls pages, stores an index of them and answers queries from that index
a device requiring that two words occur within a stated distance of each other
the cutting of a word to its stem, with a symbol, so that every ending is matched
items.s: Truncation: the cutting of a word to its stem, with a symbol, so that every ending is matched. The other options describe Stemming, Proximity operator, Search engine.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Miss?
o: the choosing of terms from a ready list to stand for the content of an item
a relevant item that the search failed to bring back
a service that suggests items from what a person has used before or what similar people used
a program that follows links across the web and copies pages back for indexing
items.s: Miss: a relevant item that the search failed to bring back. The other options describe Assignment indexing, Recommender system, Crawler.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Narrower heading?
o: the publishing of descriptions as web identifiers that other systems can follow
one complete entry in a file, made up of several separate fields
the unwanted material that appears among the results of a search
a class of more limited meaning that falls inside a wider class
items.s: Narrower heading: a class of more limited meaning that falls inside a wider class. The other options describe Linked data, Noise, Record.

items.q: Boolean NOT may be defined as
o: an approach that estimates the chance that a document is wanted from the terms it shares with the query
a word or phrase chosen from a document to represent its content in the file
the operator that removes from the result every record containing the excluded term
all the records a given search returned
items.s: Boolean NOT: the operator that removes from the result every record containing the excluded term. The other options describe Index term, Retrieved set, Probabilistic model.

items.q: Which term is described by “a service that runs a stored query at intervals and reports anything newly added”?
o: Concept block
Search strategy
Saved search
Alert
items.s: Alert is a service that runs a stored query at intervals and reports anything newly added.

items.q: Which term is described by “one element of a topic, around which synonyms are gathered before they are joined”?
o: Alert
Most specific first
Search strategy
Concept block
items.s: Concept block is one element of a topic, around which synonyms are gathered before they are joined.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Linked data?
o: a method that begins with the narrowest term and broadens only if too little is found
the number of times a given word occurs inside one document
the publishing of descriptions as web identifiers that other systems can follow
the making of scholarly writings freely readable online without a subscription
items.s: Linked data: the publishing of descriptions as web identifiers that other systems can follow. The other options describe Open access, Term frequency, Most specific first.

items.q: Which term is described by “a structured file of records that can be searched and updated independently of the programs using it”?
o: Factual databank
Retrieval system
Database
Bibliographic file
items.s: Database is a structured file of records that can be searched and updated independently of the programs using it.

a system rule that records are returned in order of how well each resembles the query
a score that treats a site as important when other important sites point to it
the publishing of descriptions as web identifiers that other systems can follow
items.s: Best match: a system rule that records are returned in order of how well each resembles the query. The other options describe Entry term, Link popularity, Linked data.

items.q: Factual databank may be defined as

a store of discrete values such as prices or properties, searched for the values themselves
a fixed set of documents, queries and agreed judgements used to compare systems
the searching of many separate collections at once through a single interface

items.s: Deep web: the material held behind forms and logins that crawling programs cannot reach. The other options describe Recall, Full text file, Field searching.

the searching of many separate collections at once through a single interface
a single front end that searches the catalogue, the repositories and the subscribed databases together
the operator that keeps records in which any one of the joined terms appears

the statement of what is wanted, expressed in the language the system can accept

Geometric similarity

a store arranged by word, listing for each word the documents that contain it
all the records a given search returned
the assignment of terms to items by a program rather than by a person
items.s: Relevance ranking: the placing of results in an order that reflects their estimated usefulness to the enquirer. The other options describe Inverted file, Machine indexing, Retrieved set.

items.q: Which term is described by “the choosing of terms from a ready list to stand for the content of an item”?
o: Indexing
Assignment indexing
Exhaustivity
Derived indexing
items.s: Assignment indexing is the choosing of terms from a ready list to stand for the content of an item.

Boolean OR
Boolean AND
Truncation

a single front end that searches the catalogue, the repositories and the subscribed databases together
the extent to which every topic touched on in an item is given a term
the shaping of results by what is known about the individual making the request

Field searching
Saved search
Concept block

Recall
Recall-precision trade-off

Relevance judgement

a structured file of records that can be searched and updated independently of the programs using it

Cosine similarity
Relevance feedback

the extent to which every topic touched on in an item is given a term
the drawing of index entries directly out of the words of the title or text
items.s: Consistency: the agreement of different indexers, or of one indexer at different times, on the terms chosen. The other options describe Exhaustivity, Derived indexing, Abstractor.

the measured extent to which two people assign the same terms to the same item
the person who writes the summary that accompanies a record in a file
the closeness of the chosen term to the exact matter treated

Alert
Concept block
